title: 2005 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: An equiangular octagon has four sides of length \(1\) and four sides of length \(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\) arranged so that no two consecutive sides have the same length. What is the area of the octagon?

solutions.text:
Extend the four sides of length \(1\) to form a square. Each short side \(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\) is the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle with legs \(\dfrac{1}{2},\) and cutting these four corners from a square of side \(1 + 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 2\) gives the octagon. Its area is \(2^2 - 4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 4 - \frac{1}{2} = \dfrac{7}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Every interior angle of an equiangular octagon is \(135^\circ;\) enclose the octagon in a larger square
The four short sides are hypotenuses of isosceles right triangles with legs \(\frac{1}{2},\) cut from a square of side \(2\)
